claim: Oxford MSc thesis proposes a structured capabilities model that separates capability from model scale and measurement error to improve construct validity of LLM benchmark results.
stance_target: measurement-theory framing of LLM evaluation (F, benchmark-level)
scope_conditions: OpenLLM Leaderboard; benchmark-level capabilities not confidence calibration
quoted_support: This thesis presents the structured capabilities model, the first model to extract interpretable and generalisable capabilities from a large collection of LLM benchmark results.

breadth.benchmarks: OpenLLM Leaderboard results; latent factor and scaling-law models (abstract, Ch. 3-4)
breadth.calibration_metrics: not present as ECE; 'calibrated to construct' used in measurement-theory sense (Sec 1.4)

claim: Measurement-theory vocabulary (construct validity, measurement error, convergent/discriminant validity) is applied to benchmark scores, not to confidence or calibration.
quoted_support: Ideally, an indicator would be perfectly calibrated to the construct it intends to measure.
